common_instruction: This is a response-only exercise. Use the supplied scenario and snippets; propose or review the requested work without claiming files were changed, commands ran, or external systems were inspected. State material verification limits. Equivalent solutions that satisfy the stated contract are acceptable.

cases.name: unavailable-does-not-prove-side-effect-absent
cases.prompt: Review a Go gRPC client's proposed retry policy. ChargeCard changes external payment state. The server may finish charging and then fail to deliver the response; in this fixture that path can return codes.Unavailable. There is no idempotency key or charge-status lookup in the accepted API. The proposal retries Unavailable three times because it means a transient error. The client already shares a connection and uses a five-second deadline. Explain what can safely be changed now and what contract is missing before automatic retries can be enabled.
expectations: Identifies the ambiguous result: Unavailable does not establish that the charge did not occur.
Does not automatically retry this operation under the supplied contract.
Names an explicit idempotency/deduplication or authoritative reconciliation contract as necessary before safe automatic retries, without pretending it already exists.
Preserves existing deadline and connection reuse; distinguishes bounded waiting from duplicate-side-effect prevention.
negative_expectations: Must not call retries safe solely because the status is Unavailable or a retry count/deadline is bounded.
Must not invent an implemented idempotency key or status endpoint and report the existing operation safe.
cases.trap: Apply a generic retryable-status table to a non-idempotent operation whose outcome may already have committed.

cases.name: in-memory-transport-test-is-not-production-deployment
cases.prompt: Plan a focused Go test for an existing gRPC service. It must check that a missing user becomes codes.NotFound after real protobuf serialization and the configured unary interceptors. The test runs entirely within one process and may use grpc/test/bufconn; no external port, Kubernetes cluster, or production credentials are available. Production TLS configuration is already covered elsewhere. Show the important setup and assertions, without claiming execution.
expectations: Uses an in-process real gRPC server/client transport such as bufconn, rather than calling the handler directly and calling that a transport test.
Includes the relevant service registration/interceptors and asserts the client-observed status code.
Bounds and cleans up client/server/listener lifetime.
Keeps any test-only insecure transport explicitly confined to the in-memory test.
negative_expectations: Must not require a Kubernetes deployment, external listener, or production certificate provisioning to perform this test.
Must not weaken or claim to verify production TLS on the strength of this fixture.
cases.trap: Confuse a bounded in-memory transport check with production deployment requirements, or replace the transport seam with a direct handler call.
